mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: When a statement equates two differences, preserve the order of subtraction on each side, treating both sides as signed expressions (e.g., (A - B) = (C - D)). This avoids converting differences to absolute values.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence of the form "the number of X that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of X that C and D have" appears.
mathgap.example: Treating (A - B) = (C - D) as |A - B| = |C - D|, which loses sign information.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's numeric value becomes known, substitute it into all pending equations and propagate the implications, iteratively reducing the system until no further values can be derived.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving a direct count, a comparative equation, a transfer that yields a numeric value, or any other constraint that fixes a variable.
mathgap.example: Leaving a known variable unchanged in other equations, missing the chance to deduce additional counts.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Evaluate each comparative statement using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative, after applying all earlier statements (including transfers and direct counts).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing any "more/fewer" comparison or a difference‑equality that appears in the text.
mathgap.example: Using initial counts for a comparison that appears after a transfer, thereby ignoring the effect of the transfer.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the minimal set of variables and equations that are directly or indirectly connected to the queried person, and ignore unrelated statements to keep the solving effort tractable.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Before solving, after parsing all statements, to focus on the relevant subsystem for the final question.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire large system, including many unrelated variables, which adds unnecessary complexity.

mathgap.title: Distinct Name Disambiguation
mathgap.principle: Treat each unique capitalized token as a separate variable, even if names differ by only a single character or resemble common nouns, to avoid accidental merging.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing the list of persons, ensure every distinct name gets its own variable.
mathgap.example: Merging "Micheal" and "Michael" into one variable, causing incorrect equations.

mathgap.title: Preserve Order in "Difference Between" Phrases
mathgap.principle: Interpret phrases like "the difference between the number of X that A and B have" as the signed subtraction A − B, preserving the order of the names as given.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When parsing any "difference between" clause on either side of an equality.
mathgap.example: Interpreting "difference between A and B" as |A − B|, thereby losing sign information.

mathgap.title: General Comparative Interpretation (more/fewer)
mathgap.principle: Interpret "A has K more (fewer) items than B" as the signed equation A − B = K (or = ‑K for fewer), preserving sign and direction.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When encountering a comparative statement containing the words "more" or "fewer".
mathgap.example: Swapping the direction and writing B − A = K, which reverses the sign.

mathgap.title: Direct Count Handling with Overrides
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X has N items", set X's count to N at that point, overriding any previous value (including after earlier transfers or comparisons).
mathgap.when_to_apply: When processing a direct count statement.
mathgap.example: Treating a later "X has N" as an additional constraint rather than resetting X's count, leading to contradictions.

mathgap.title: Chronological Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: Apply each transfer (e.g., "X gives K items to Y") in the order they appear, updating both donor and recipient counts immediately; if a count is unknown, treat the transfer as a pending equation to be resolved later.
mathgap.example: Applying transfers out of order, which yields incorrect intermediate counts.

mathgap.title: Transfer as Equation for Unknown Counts
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement involves a donor or recipient whose count is not yet known, represent the transfer as a linear equation (donor = donor - K, recipient = recipient + K) and keep it pending; later, once the count becomes known, substitute and propagate.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a "X gives K items to Y" appears and X or Y lacks a numeric count at that moment.
mathgap.example: Skipping the transfer because the donor's count is unknown, thereby losing a constraint on the system.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in 'has K more than' statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model misinterprets the phrase and reverses the subtraction order.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always map "A has K more than B" to A - B = K, not B - A = K.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model drops sign information when converting "difference between" phrases.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the order of subtraction; do not take absolute values.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model applies transfers after solving all equations, losing intermediate effects.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply each transfer immediately when it appears in the narrative.

mathgap.description: Treating 'has N' as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes direct counts are immutable base values.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Override any previous value for a person when a direct count statement is encountered, respecting chronology.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model multiplies a count before the base value is established.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Only apply multiplicative increases after the current count is known.
